user.title: ZKSJ wave pump
user.description:
How should Home Assistant reach the pump?

**Cloud (MQTT)** is the one that works on the wave pump: it ignores local control entirely and only accepts commands through Tuya's broker, which is what the vendor app uses too. Needs credentials read out of the app once.

**Local** talks to the pump directly on your own network. Try it only if you have a pump or firmware that answers it.

menu_options.cloud: Cloud (MQTT) — recommended for the wave pump

cloud.title: Cloud (MQTT) connection
cloud.description:
These all come from one capture of the vendor app's own session — see docs/ZKSJ.md for how to take it.

The username, password, client id and source id are **session-scoped**: they stop working when that session ends, and there is no way to renew them without the app. When the pump goes unavailable, take a fresh capture and paste the new values into Reconfigure.

local.title: ZKSJ wave pump
local.description: These are the Tuya devices broadcasting on your network. Pick your pump; you will only need to paste its local key.

key.title: Local key
key.description:
Found the pump at {host} (device id {device_id}).

Paste its local key for full control. **Leave it blank** to add the pump in monitor-only mode: you get a Connection sensor showing whether it has power and is on the network, and nothing else — reading its mode, speed or on/off state is not possible without the key. You can add the key later with Reconfigure.

manual.title: Enter the pump by hand
manual.description: No pump was found broadcasting, or you chose to type it in. Find the address with `python -m tinytuya scan`. Leave the local key blank for monitor-only mode.

reconfigure_cloud.title: Refresh the MQTT session
reconfigure_cloud.description: The broker credentials are session-scoped and expire; replacing them is the normal upkeep of a cloud pump, not a sign anything is broken. Take a fresh capture of the app's session and paste the new values.

reconfigure_local.title: Update pump connection
reconfigure_local.description: Point Home Assistant at a new address, add a local key to a monitor-only pump, or replace a key that changed after re-pairing. Clearing the key returns the pump to monitor-only.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the pump. On a cloud entry this almost always means the MQTT credentials have expired — take a fresh capture of the app's session. On a local entry, check the local key first: a wrong key looks exactly like this.
error.unknown: Unexpected error while contacting the pump.

abort.already_configured: This pump is already set up.

feed.name: Feed mode
feed.description: Slows the pump for feeding. The pump runs the countdown itself and returns to its program.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long feed mode lasts, in seconds.

power.name: Flow
power.description: Flow to hold during feed mode, as a percentage.

set_program.name: Set program
set_program.description: Replaces the pump's whole daily program with a list of segments.

segments.name: Segments
segments.description: Segments, each with a wave type, a start and end time, and its flow, frequency and duty cycle.

sync_time.name: Sync clock
sync_time.description: Pushes Home Assistant's local time to the pump, so time-based programs run at the right hour.
